the administration of endothelial-like cells to rats with established monocrotaline-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension results in improved pulmonary hemodynamics, microvascular structure, and survival.

we have shown that progenitor cells can be used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension, but the best results were obtained when the progenitor cells were genetically modified to overexpress endothelial nitric oxide synthase.
